question: In which of the following years did the Reserve Bank of India introduce a comprehensive regulatory framework for Non-Banking Finance Company - Micro Finance Institutions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2011**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on April 1, 1935.
 
• It was initially set up based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission.
 
• The original headquarters of RBI was located in Kolkata, but it was permanently moved to Mumbai in 1937.
 
• The RBI was initially set up as a private entity but was nationalized in 1949 after India's independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hilton Young Commission

 
 
• The Hilton Young Commission, also known as the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, was set up in 1926 to investigate and recommend changes to the monetary system in India.
 
• The commission recommended the establishment of a central bank to manage India's currency and credit, which led to the formation of the RBI.
 
 
 
• Functions of RBI
 
 
• The RBI acts as the regulator of the entire financial system in India, ensuring its stability and efficiency.
 
• It manages the country's currency and monetary policy and serves as the banker to the government and other banks.
 
• The RBI also oversees the foreign exchange market and maintains the foreign exchange reserves of India.
 
 
 
• Nationalization of RBI
 
 
• In 1949, the Reserve Bank of India was nationalized, meaning it was taken over by the government of India.
 
• This step was taken to ensure a greater degree of control over the credit and monetary policy, aligning it with the nation's economic interests.
 
 
 
• Role in Economic Development
 
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in the economic development of India through its monetary policies, regulation of financial institutions, and management of the payment system.
 
• It also focuses on financial inclusion, aiming to make financial services accessible to the unbanked and underbanked population.
